title: ChatCompletions compatibility adapter: robust mapping for streaming + function/tool calls
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Several Redwood customers call our Chat API expecting OpenAI ChatCompletions wire format and semantics. While we already support naive field translation, complex real-world usage shows gaps: streaming function/tool calls are emitted as fragmented deltas (function name and arguments split across several chunks); finish_reason/stop semantics differ; structured outputs validated against JSON schemas can be broken across stream fragments; and clients rely on legacy behavior like explicit 'function' roles and finish_reason == 'function_call'.

Goal: Implement a robust compatibility adapter that translates between Redwood internal streaming model messages and the OpenAI ChatCompletions request/response model, correctly handling: full and partial function/tool calls across streaming chunks, incremental assembly and validation of function arguments (possibly malformed mid-stream), mapping finish_reason/stop semantics, preserving role/name metadata, and producing both streaming delta events and final choice objects that match OpenAI expectations. This should be resilient to truncated or duplicated chunks, support both auto and forced function_call modes, and include observability hooks for serialization/validation failures.

Scope: adapter for request/response mapping and streaming; does not include UI console changes. Deliver code path, tests, and rollout with feature flag.

Out-of-scope: changing underlying model runtime, changing customer-facing API surface beyond compatibility mapping, or migrating old persisted logs to new schema.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming delta events produced by Redwood are mapped to OpenAI-style 'delta' chunks where clients incrementally receive role/content fragments and function_call fragments in the same order they would with OpenAI's stream.

Function/tool calls that are emitted across multiple streaming chunks are deterministically assembled into a single choice.function_call object with fully concatenated 'arguments' string, and the final response includes function_call.name and function_call.arguments when finish_reason is 'function_call'.

If function_call arguments are malformed JSON after assembly, the adapter marks the choice with 'schema_error' in logs and provides the best-effort raw arguments string in the final choice, without dropping the event mid-stream.

finish_reason mapping: Redwood stop/complete/error states map to OpenAI finish_reason values ("stop", "function_call", "length", "error"). Streaming clients receive a final delta with an explicit 'finish_reason' or an end-of-stream sentinel that clients expect from OpenAI streams.

Structured-output (JSON-schema) responses are validated server-side after stream completion; validation results are recorded in request-level diagnostics and returned as a non-breaking annotation (not changing tokens) so compatibility consumers can still parse a final choice object.
Backward-compat: requests specifying OpenAI-style 'function_call': 'auto' | 'none' | {name} are honored and routed to the runtime; adapter does not alter caller intent.
New behavior is guarded by a feature flag and can be rolled back; no increase in 5xx rate or request latency beyond 5% in alpha traffic.
Comprehensive unit + integration tests cover chunked function arguments, duplicate chunks, truncated streams, and concurrent requests assembling multiple function calls.
technical_notes: Maintain per-request streaming state machine with these slots: role (first non-empty role observed), content_buffer (string), function_call_buffer.name (first emitted name), function_call_buffer.arguments (append contiguous argument fragments), last_emit_seq (counter).

Use a small deterministic reassembly policy: ignore duplicate consecutive token fragments if identical to last_emit_seq; tolerate overlapping fragments by idempotent append operations with optional checksum detection (sha1 of arguments buffer) to detect accidental replays.

When receiving function_call fragments, treat 'name' as sticky once set for the request. If later fragments change the name, mark as 'name_conflict' in diagnostics and prefer the first non-empty name (documented behavior).

Do not attempt to parse/validate partial JSON for function_call.arguments until end-of-stream; instead accumulate raw UTF-8 bytes. After stream completes, attempt JSON.parse with a tolerant mode: if parse fails due to trailing commas or single quotes, run a best-effort sanitizer pass and attempt parse again. If still fails, return raw string and emit a 'schema_error' tag in diagnostics.

Map Redwood internal finish signals: INTERNAL_COMPLETE -> finish_reason 'stop'; INTERNAL_FUNCTION_HOOK -> 'function_call'; INTERNAL_TRUNCATED -> 'length'; INTERNAL_ERROR -> 'error'. Include original internal code in telemetry.
Expose a small compatibility header (X-Compat-Mode: openai-chat) so downstream proxies and analytics can opt-in to OpenAI mapping logic; default disabled until rollout.
Implement as an adapter layer inside the API gateway (pre-serialize) to avoid touching runtime kernels; minimal latency impact targeted (<2ms median added).
test_plan: Unit tests for the state machine: sequences of simulated stream deltas that include (a) complete single-chunk function_call, (b) multi-chunk function_call args, (c) duplicated chunk replays, (d) truncated streams, (e) conflicting function name updates.

Integration test using a stubbed runtime that emits OpenAI-like streaming deltas; assert final choice objects equal expected OpenAI ChatCompletions response structure for a matrix of function_call modes and schema scenarios.
Fuzz tests: random split points for valid JSON function args to ensure reassembly is robust; property tests should assert idempotence under duplicate fragments.

Performance tests: measure p50/p95 added latency for adapter in alpha mode versus baseline and assert <5% p95 regression. Monitor memory usage for long-lived accumulation buffers to avoid OOM on large argument payloads.
Security tests: ensure special characters and byte sequences in arguments cannot cause injection at logging/console; sanitize diagnostics outputs. Coordinate with security review.
rollout_plan: Merge behind feature flag 'compat-openai-chat'. Enable for internal-only traffic and run smoke tests for 24h.
Enable for 5% production traffic for 48h; monitor errors (schema_error rate, 5xx), latency, and user-facing integrity metrics (mismatched choice.count, missing function_call).
Progress to 25% for 72h if metrics stable, then 100% in 1 week. Rollback toggle available in gateway with immediate effect.
If high schema_error or 5xx regressions observed, automatically disable and create emergency rollback incident runbook.
